title_zh: 第二十三類 法術騙

stories.title_en: A Monk Fakes Reflections in Water and Plots Rebellion

paragraphs.zh: 僧術中有以法咒水密咒某人，心欲何事，後令人自取照之，各隨其心之所欲，自現其形。有米春元者，富過百萬，田連兩府，年逾五十，不思會試，唯安享豪華以為樂。妖僧聞其富，欲騙其厚利也，挾咒水之術，往叩其門，自言能望氣，每見此宅紫氣上沖，有鸞鳳之彩。此百代王侯之兆，當有立翊運之功、分河山之帶礪者。米春元未信。僧曰：「吾傳有秘術，以符咒水能知此生榮枯結果。人但齋戒三日，虔心來照，則今生是何成就，自現於水中。」米乃留此僧，令家下人各齋戒。
paragraphs.en: Among monastic arts there is one that uses a method of cursing water, secretly cursing a certain person: whatever the heart desires, afterward they have the person take and look at it himself, and each, following what the heart wants, has his own form appear. There was one Mi Chunyuan, rich beyond a million, with fields joining two prefectures, past fifty, with no thought of sitting the metropolitan examination, only taking ease and luxury as his pleasure. A demonic monk heard of his wealth and wanted to cheat him of thick profit. Carrying the art of cursed water, he went and knocked at his gate, saying of himself that he could watch qi: he always saw purple qi rising from this house, with the colors of simurgh and phoenix. This was an omen of kings and lords for a hundred generations; there should be those who would establish the merit of assisting the dynasty’s fortune, and share the rivers and mountains under pledges of enfeoffment. Mi Chunyuan did not yet believe. The monk said, “I have transmitted a secret art. With talismans and cursed water one can know this life’s glory and withering and its end. A person need only fast three days, come with a devout heart to look, and what this life’s achievement is will of itself appear in the water.” Mi then kept this monk, and ordered everyone in the household to fast.

paragraphs.zh: 至第三日，注大缸水於庭。僧密語咒水，令諸人自照。米照見戴丫天冠，穿蟒袍。幼子照之，亦同。長次二子，只紗帽圓領而已。米正室照，亦妃冠鳳袍。兩長婦照，唯珠冠翟服。米大異之，僅秘於心。
paragraphs.en: On the third day they poured a large vat of water in the courtyard. The monk secretly spoke a curse over the water, and had everyone look for themselves. Mi looked and saw himself wearing a forked heavenly crown and python robes. His youngest son looked, and it was the same. The two elder sons had only gauze hats and round-collared robes. Mi’s principal wife looked, and she too had a consort’s crown and phoenix robes. The two elder daughters-in-law looked, and had only pearl crowns and pheasant-patterned dress. Mi thought it greatly strange, and only kept it secret in his heart.

paragraphs.zh: 後與流寓枝鄉官宴會，談及時事，枝曰：「今併後匹敵，金注支庶。禍之萌，必始宮闈。異日不為文皇之蹀血，或為沂王府之反召。此魯嫠所深卹者。」米曰：「往者逆未萌而折，宸豪已發而摧。國家如天之福，風雨何搖於牖戶也？」枝曰：「不然。文靜以監豎倡唐，姚衍以胖僧興國。若輔之得人，成敗安可料也？」米曰：「縱中土有故，水國偏在海隅，必無憂亂離也。」枝曰：「亦難保。讖云『某地出天子，江南作戰場』，正可慮也。」米曰：「使宸豪復興於今，成敗當何如？」枝曰：「今承平馳兵，更甚於昔。向令宸豪不久淹南康，某都不詐應反戈，安至以銅鐘灰也？」米聞言心喜。
paragraphs.en: Later, at a banquet with Zhi, a local official living away from his post, they talked of current affairs. Zhi said, “Now after combining they stand as matched rivals, and the gold is staked on the junior branches. The sprout of disaster will surely begin in the palace. One day it will be either the Yongle Emperor’s trampling in blood, or the rebellious summons of the Prince of Yi’s household. This is what the widow of Lu deeply worried over.” Mi said, “In the past, rebellion was snapped before it sprouted, and Chenhao, once he had risen, was crushed. The state’s fortune is like Heaven’s. How can wind and rain shake door and window?” Zhi said, “Not so. Wenjing raised Tang by means of eunuchs; Yao Yan founded a state by means of a fat monk. If they obtain the right helpers, how can success or failure be predicted?” Mi said, “Even if the central lands have trouble, this watery country lies off in a sea corner. There is surely no worry of chaos and separation.” Zhi said, “That too is hard to guarantee. A prophecy says, ‘A Son of Heaven will come forth from a certain place; Jiangnan will be a battlefield.’ That is exactly what is to be feared.” Mi said, “If Chenhao rose again today, what would success or failure be?” Zhi said, “Now in long peace the troops have gone slack, still more than in the past. If in those days Chenhao had not lingered long at Nankang, and a certain capital had not falsely answered and then turned their spears, how would it have come to copper-bell ashes?” Mi heard this and was pleased in his heart.

paragraphs.zh: 又有一僧，能降神附童者，言往來禍福，如聲應響。米請降之密禱，以欲圖不軌事。神降曰：「金鍾興，玉氣旺，清福扶王帝業強。洪流掃蕩人安泰，裂土移宮鎮遠方。」米猶未決休咎，再求明報。降童喝曰：「此何事而敢絮叨也！」米不敢問，而未解神意。既而漁人於深淵得巨鐘，金色燁然。米以為瑞也，召枝某及二僧決謀逆，欲俟五月某日五更早，大小官俱出城送萬壽表，乃閉四門，伏兵城外，悉殲之。
paragraphs.en: There was also another monk who could bring down a spirit to possess a boy, speaking of coming misfortunes and blessings like an echo answering a sound. Mi asked him to bring it down and prayed in secret, about wanting to plot an unlawful matter. The spirit descended and said: “The golden bell arises, jade qi flourishes; clear fortune supports the king, the imperial enterprise is strong. A great flood sweeps clean, people are at peace; split the land, move the palace, garrison the far regions.” Mi still had not decided good or ill, and again asked for a clear report. The possessed boy shouted, “What matter is this, that you dare chatter on!” Mi dared not ask, and still did not understand the spirit’s meaning. Soon after, a fisherman in a deep pool got a huge bell, gleaming gold. Mi took it as an omen. He summoned Zhi and the two monks to decide on plotting rebellion, meaning to wait until a certain day in the fifth month, at the fifth watch in the morning, when officials great and small would all leave the city to send off the imperial-longevity memorial, then close the four gates, ambush troops outside the city, and wipe them all out.

paragraphs.zh: 至四更，兵卒供執事者早起，見城內伏兵處燈火異常，急報軍官調兵捕之。城中擾亂，又遣兵守城。見江中船無數，皆早炊飯。城上兵疑是助亂者，大呼曰：「某人謀逆，被捕獲斬首矣！」外伏者見內無號砲，城上有備，又聞呼喊聲，送表官皆不出城，知事必敗露，河邊數十號船，乘微明時各各逃散。後官以亂者作造謀反劫庫問，捕獲數十餘人，皆斬首。而首逆者，反以不知情為辭，只擬流三千里而死於道。
paragraphs.en: At the fourth watch, soldiers and those on duty rose early, saw unusual lamps and fires at the places of ambush inside the city, and urgently reported to the officers, who deployed troops to arrest them. The city was in disorder, and they also sent troops to guard the walls. They saw countless boats on the river, all cooking breakfast early. The soldiers on the walls suspected they were aiding the rebels, and shouted, “So-and-so has plotted rebellion, been captured and beheaded!” Those ambushed outside saw no signal cannon from within, the walls were prepared, and they also heard the shouting. The officials sending the memorial all did not leave the city. They knew the matter must have come to light. Dozens of boats by the river, taking the faint light, each fled and scattered. Later officials treated the rebels as having plotted rebellion and robbery of the treasury. They captured several dozen men, all beheaded. The chief rebel, on the contrary, used not knowing as his plea, and was only sentenced to exile three thousand li, and died on the road.

paragraphs.zh: 按：米春元年老巨富，已無心向功名，更何心圖王侯？止以咒水妖僧啟其端，降神妖僧決其志，又以枝某失職，怏怏釀成大逆。二僧已就誅，而枝某幸脫於網。天何緩討凶人哉？猶幸聖朝清明，小丑旋殄，固太平之洪福，亦此地民風素良善忠順，不當受此叛逆者之荼毒也。然信僧惑邪之禍亦酷矣。後人其深鑑之，其深戒之。
paragraphs.en: Note: Mi Chunyuan was old and hugely rich, already with no heart toward rank and fame—still less what heart to plot to be a king or lord? Only the cursed-water demonic monk opened the beginning, the spirit-descending demonic monk decided his resolve, and also Zhi, out of office, resentful, brewed a great treason. The two monks had already been put to death, and Zhi luckily slipped the net. Why is Heaven slow to punish the wicked? Still, fortunately the sagely court is clear and bright, and the petty rebels were quickly wiped out. This was truly the great fortune of peace, and also this place’s folkways have always been good, loyal, and obedient, and they ought not to have suffered the poison of these rebels. Yet the disaster of believing monks and being confused by heresy is also cruel. Later people, deeply take this as a mirror; deeply take this as a warning.

stories.title_en: Sorcery Sends a Dream, Then They Rob the House

paragraphs.zh: 老狐晝伏岩洞，夜出尋食草木之實。有偶於草木中吸得天地氤氳之情者，便有靈變，能幻化為美婦，以迷誘人，採人之陽精，以益其靈通。法師捕得而烹之。和尚如求得狐心，焙而乾之，熏以好香，於深山中構一草廬，以狐心奉祀於中，日誦諸般懺文經卷超度之，夜則群妖眾怪嗥者、呼者、悲者、泣者、叫者、嘯者、能為人言或蠻語者，千怪萬狀，於草廬外哀弔，極其淒涼。要極大膽之人，方敢中處。弔過七日，亦漸漸稀少。晝夜常誦經作法，備果食供奉。積至四十九日，然後焚了草廬，把狐心領回，香火祀之。如明日欲往見某人，先夜以錦囊盛狐心，置於心上，夜必夢婦人領之，先見其人：次日往拜其人，已夢中相會。後有所干求，人必以為異而多從之。此僧家騙化之一術也。
paragraphs.en: Old foxes hide by day in cliff caves, and at night go out seeking the fruits of plants. Those that happen among the plants to draw in the generative breath of Heaven and Earth then have spiritual change. They can transform into beautiful women to bewitch and lure men, taking a man’s yang essence to increase their spiritual power. When a ritual master captures one and cooks it, if a monk obtains the fox’s heart, he roasts it dry, fumigates it with good incense, builds a thatched hut in the deep mountains, and enshrines the fox heart in it. By day he recites all kinds of repentance texts and sutra scrolls to deliver it. At night then crowds of demons and monsters—those that howl, those that call, those that grieve, those that weep, those that shout, those that whistle, those that can speak human words or barbarian speech—a thousand strange forms, mourn outside the hut, extremely desolate. Only a person of the greatest courage dares stay in the middle. After seven days of mourning they also gradually thin. Day and night he constantly recites sutras and works magic, and prepares fruit and food as offerings. When it has accumulated to forty-nine days, he then burns the thatched hut, takes the fox heart back, and worships it with incense and fire. If tomorrow he wants to go see a certain person, the night before he puts the fox heart in a brocade bag and places it on his heart. At night he will surely dream a woman leads him, and he first sees that person. The next day he goes to pay respects to that person, and they have already met in a dream. Afterward, whatever he seeks, people will surely find it strange and often comply. This is one art of monks’ fraudulent collecting.

paragraphs.zh: 有富家羊老，生二子娶二媳矣。蓄積盈餘，極是慳吝，分文不肯施捨。忽夜夢兩高僧來化緣，次日果有兩僧到，容貌儼如夢中所會者，稱言：「你取財太急，人多怨氣。吾與你有夙緣，特來為你懺悔。」羊老信之，問：「懺悔當如何？」僧曰：「你合家當齋戒三日，再買果餅麵食及三牲豬羊肉，半葷半素，吾為你作法請將，誦經供佛，將生前罪過解釋，再祈後增福祿，便家門請吉，死後免墮矣。」羊老依言，齋戒買辦。
paragraphs.en: There was a rich house, Yang-lao. He had two sons and had already married two daughters-in-law. His stores were more than enough, but he was extremely stingy, and would not give a single cash. Suddenly at night he dreamed two eminent monks came collecting alms. The next day two monks indeed arrived, their looks exactly like those he had met in the dream. They said, “You take wealth too urgently. People have much resentful qi. We have a former-life tie with you, and have come specially to repent for you.” Yang-lao believed them, and asked, “How should the repentance be done?” The monks said, “Your whole family should fast three days, then buy fruit, cakes, flour foods, and the three sacrificial meats of pig and sheep, half meat and half vegetarian. We will work magic for you, invite spirit-generals, recite sutras and offer to the Buddha, dissolve the sins of your lifetime, then pray that afterward blessings and emoluments increase, so the household will be fortunate, and after death you will be spared falling.” Yang-lao followed their words, fasted, and bought the things.

paragraphs.zh: 至第三日，又有兩僧到，又留相助誦經。至晚，來一僧念咒燒符，降遣羊老自跳自喊，取利劍在手，指其妻、子曰：「此鬼也。」悉手刃之。又追殺二媳。媳求僧解勸。僧指羊老喝曰：「坐！」羊老遂提劍咬牙，昏昏而坐，不醒人事。四僧入，輪姦二婦訖，以索縛之。搜其家財幣，捆作四擔，夤夜逃去。
paragraphs.en: On the third day two more monks arrived, and were also kept to help recite sutras. That evening a monk came, chanted spells and burned talismans, and sent Yang-lao jumping and shouting. He took a sharp sword in his hand, pointed at his wife and sons, and said, “These are ghosts.” He cut them all down with his own hand. Then he chased and tried to kill the two daughters-in-law. The daughters-in-law begged the monks to intervene and persuade. A monk pointed at Yang-lao and shouted, “Sit!” Yang-lao then held the sword, grinding his teeth, sat in a daze, and was not conscious. The four monks went in, raped the two women in turn, then bound them with rope. They searched the house for money and goods, packed four loads, and fled in the dead of night.

paragraphs.zh: 次日，有人入其家者，見羊老被髮伏劍，睜眼語，急出呼眾入看。親眾群擁而入，羊老只說要殺鬼。眾向前奪去其劍，呼其名曰：「你何故如此？」羊老漸漸復蘇。人又問之，才知應曰：「吾夢見鬼多，正在此殺鬼，得你們叫我醒也。」及入後室，妻與子皆被殺。羊老大哭曰：「此我記得，殺三鬼在此，又趕殺二鬼婆，被僧攔開。」及入房，二婦皆捆在床，乃呼鄰婦來解之。各稱被僧所姦，金銀財帛皆收拾去矣。一家痛恨無窮，一邊收殮三尸，一邊遣人四路趕僧，皆趕上兩日路，並不見踪而還。
paragraphs.en: The next day someone who entered the house saw Yang-lao with hair loose, clutching the sword, staring and talking. He rushed out and called people in to look. Relatives crowded in. Yang-lao only said he wanted to kill ghosts. They went forward, took away his sword, and called his name: “Why are you like this?” Yang-lao gradually revived. People asked him again, and only then he answered, “I dreamed there were many ghosts, and was just killing ghosts here. You called me awake.” When they went into the back rooms, wife and sons had all been killed. Yang-lao wailed, “This I remember: I killed three ghosts here, then chased and tried to kill two ghost-women, and the monks blocked me.” When they went into the rooms, both women were bound on the beds. They then called neighbor women to untie them. Each said she had been raped by the monks, and the gold, silver, and goods had all been gathered and taken. The whole house hated without end. On one side they prepared the three corpses for burial; on the other they sent people on four roads to chase the monks. All chased two days’ journey, saw no trace at all, and came back.

paragraphs.zh: 按：羊老素慳吝，則為富不仁之事有矣。乃僧悚以怨氣，便信其說，而留以作福懺悔，則心先自疚故也。僧欲行術劫財，而先形於夢，此亦得狐心引夢之術而用之。彼夢謂高僧而反為劫僧，不信晝所為而信夜所夢，亦惑矣；不行善於平昔，而求懺悔於修齋，亦愚矣。今人多殘忍不仁，貪暴不義，而欲飯僧供佛，追修懺悔，何異羊老之覆哉！甚矣！惡不可為，而僧不可信也。鑑此當為之凜凜。
paragraphs.en: Note: Yang-lao was always stingy, so there were surely deeds of being rich without benevolence. Then the monks frightened him with resentful qi, he believed their talk, and kept them to make blessings and repent—because the heart first felt guilty of itself. The monks wanted to work arts and rob wealth, and first took form in a dream. This too was obtaining the fox-heart art of leading dreams and using it. He dreamed they were eminent monks, and they turned out instead to be robber-monks. Not believing what is done by day, but believing what is dreamed by night, is also delusion. Not doing good in ordinary times, but seeking repentance in keeping a fast, is also folly. Today many people are cruel and unbenevolent, greedy and unjust, yet want to feed monks and offer to the Buddha, pursue cultivation and repentance. How is that different from Yang-lao’s overturning? Extreme indeed! Evil must not be done, and monks must not be believed. Seeing this, one should tremble.

stories.title_en: The Face-Stroking Thief Abducts Young Boys

paragraphs.zh: 往年，京城中有幼童出外，嘗被人拐帶而去，尋之又無踪。後累累有之。人多見一僧，摩幼童之臉，則幼童隨之而行。既而尋，已失之。故京城盛傳謂之「摩臉賊」。時在京僧釋人多，未察其孰是也。
paragraphs.en: In past years, in the capital, young boys who went out were often abducted and taken away; when people searched, there was again no trace. Later this happened again and again. Many people saw a monk stroke a young boy’s face, and then the boy followed him and walked. When they searched soon after, he was already lost. So the capital widely called him the “face-stroking thief.” At the time there were many monks in the capital, and they had not yet made out which one it was.

paragraphs.zh: 忽宓富人，止生一子，出外不返，四下跟尋甚急，各處出賞帖曰：「有收留得者，賞銀二十兩；報信者賞銀一十兩。」四出掛帖出賞，終莫得下落。
paragraphs.en: Suddenly a rich Mi family, who had only one son, had him go out and not return. They followed and searched in all directions very urgently, and put out reward notices in all places: “Anyone who has taken him in, reward twenty taels of silver; an informant, reward ten taels of silver.” They hung notices and offered rewards in all directions, and in the end never got word of him.

paragraphs.zh: 住宓家小屋人班八，以淘街為生。一日，懶去掏街，往城外晦真庵閒遊，轉入後室，四旁周覽。忽破水障中一小士露頭來。班八認是宓家人，忙呼之曰：「家中四處尋你，何故在此？」宓子曰：「僧閉禁我在此，你快來救我！」班八看房門已鎖，恐一人難帶此子出，謂之曰：「你小心暫在此，我報你令尊知，即來取你矣。」飛跑而歸，報宓老曰：「令郎受禁在晦真庵中，速去救之。」宓老即招五十餘人，前後到庵。班八引至庵後房中，打開門，認出宓子，又搜出十數童輩，即令眾人捆住僧小山並同庵三人，都縛來狀送到官。
paragraphs.en: Ban Ba, who lived in a small house of the Mi family, made a living cleaning streets. One day he was too lazy to go clean streets, went outside the city to Huizhen Hermitage to idle, turned into the back rooms, and looked all around. Suddenly a small scholar’s head showed through a broken water-screen. Ban Ba recognized him as of the Mi household, and hurriedly called, “Your family is searching for you in all four directions. Why are you here?” Mi’s son said, “The monk has locked me in here. Come save me quickly!” Ban Ba saw the door was already locked, feared one man would have a hard time taking this boy out, and said to him, “Stay careful here a while. I will report to your father, and then come get you.” He ran home at flying speed and reported to Mi-lao: “Your son is imprisoned in Huizhen Hermitage. Go save him at once.” Mi-lao at once gathered fifty-odd men, and they arrived at the hermitage from front and back. Ban Ba led them to the back room of the hermitage, broke open the door, identified Mi’s son, and also searched out a dozen other boys. He then had everyone bind the monk Xiaoshan and three others of the same hermitage. They were all tied and sent with a complaint to the officials.

paragraphs.zh: 官先審問眾童曰：「汝等如何被引入庵？」眾童曰：「和尚以手摩我眼睛，便見兩邊背後都是猛虎毒蛇，將來咬人傷人，唯面前一條路清淨好行，我輩只向前走，便到此庵，被和尚幽閉住。」又問曰：「和尚留汝等在庵幹何事？」眾童曰：「可恨這禿子，不拘日夜，將我等做苦春，極是疼痛。若不從，便將大杖撻打。眾人怕他，只得從他所為。」又問曰：「先拐來的後必長大，都放在何處去？」眾童曰：「有病者有長大者，和尚說放他回去，未知後都回家否。」官再審僧小山曰：「你拐來眾童後，病的長的都放哪裡去？」僧不敢應。再問同庵三人，都云：「毒死埋訖。」官聞言大怒，將小山打四十，同庵者各打二十，曰：「此罪不容於死。」令鎖出衙門外，許失童之家君聚手毆，打得身無完膚，有割其陽塞於僧口者，半日而死。人莫不恨其淫而快其死。後將其庵焚之，拐帶之禍遂息。
paragraphs.en: The official first questioned the boys: “How were you led into the hermitage?” The boys said, “The monk stroked our eyes with his hand, and then we saw on both sides behind us fierce tigers and venomous snakes, coming to bite and harm people. Only the one road in front was clean and good to walk. We only went forward, and then arrived at this hermitage, and were shut in by the monk.” He asked again, “What did the monk keep you in the hermitage to do?” The boys said, “Hateful, this bald one. Day or night, he used us for his lust, which was extremely painful. If we did not comply, he would beat us with a big staff. Everyone feared him, and had no choice but to do as he wanted.” He asked again, “Those abducted earlier must later have grown up. Where were they all sent?” The boys said, “Those who were sick and those who had grown up, the monk said he sent them back. We do not know whether afterward they all got home.” The official then examined the monk Xiaoshan: “After you abducted the boys, where did you send the sick ones and the grown ones?” The monk dared not answer. He asked the three of the same hermitage again; they all said, “Poisoned and buried.” The official heard this and was greatly enraged. He had Xiaoshan beaten forty strokes, and those of the same hermitage twenty each, and said, “This crime cannot be allowed to live.” He ordered them locked out in front of the yamen gate, and allowed the fathers of the lost boys to gather and beat them with their own hands. They were beaten until no skin was left whole. Some cut off his genitals and stuffed them in the monk’s mouth. He died within half a day. There was no one who did not hate his lust and rejoice at his death. Later they burned the hermitage, and the disaster of abduction then ceased.

paragraphs.zh: 按：好男風者，禽瀆之行。此僧必有春意之方，非拐諸幼童，無以快其欲。又習得妖法，摩其眼睛則昏花見怪，故可誘引童男。其罪浮於天矣。積惡貫盈，眾戮其身，言之羞口舌，書之污簡牘，人誰不切齒之！世有負男子之軀者，其可襲此僧之惡行哉！
paragraphs.en: Note: Those who love male-male relations—this is the conduct of beasts. This monk must have had a lust-enhancing method; without abducting young boys, he had no way to satisfy his desire. He also learned demonic arts: stroking their eyes, they would see darkness and monsters, so he could lure boys. His crime floats above Heaven. When accumulated evil was full, the crowd killed him. Speaking of it shames the tongue; writing it stains the pages. Who would not grind their teeth? Those in the world who bear a man’s body—how can they follow this monk’s evil conduct?
